s1_reservation_detail: Representation B provided a value for mmv:hasIdentifier, which I could not find in the data. I become wary whenever I see values that seem to come from thin air.  While B provides a lot more information, it seems to follow a method that is not apparent in the file. I wonder about the dissonance between the method/tool and the artifacts it uses. Because of this lack of knowledge, I prefer simpler metadata descriptions.
s1_useful_detail: While B has more details, I preferred A because the artefacts itself does not indicate any method.
s1_missing_detail: Had B additional metadata about the process/method, I would have chosen B. I want to clarify that I am not judging technical correctness, but merely the disconnect between the metadata descriptioin which seems to commit to a specific approach for using/adopting this mapping.
s1_comments: For this experiment, I copied/pasted the description in VS Code to beautify it. I can't read the string presented on this page.
s2_useful_detail: Compared to the previous question, where I was unsure whether the mapping came from an existing project (analysis, design, testing, ...), this question clearly specified that it came from an existing project. Hence, the sections (analysis, design, ...) made sense, and I felt comfortable relying on my decision on those.
s2_missing_detail: Both were missing licenses for the mapping, but I did appreciate that A explicitly mentioned it. The same goes for mapping authors. Some PROV-O or the like would have been useful.
s2_comments: I am unfamiliar with YARRRML, and I couldn't beautify the string provided for this exercise. Hence, I could only guess the gist of the mapping.
s3_useful_detail: While B is more structured, I was confused by the present perfect tense in some IRIs (see below). That gave me more confidence in A.
s3_missing_detail: It did not contain information about the type of mapping. Here, we had an exhaustive list of concrete correspondences (an existential approach to mappings and not an intentional one that needs to be executed). This would be interesting for all mappings "to be executed" vs. "result of an execution".
s3_comments:
mmv:hasInputType was too vague for my liking.
mmv:hasPlannedQualityMetric is confusing because the IRI label is in the present perfect tense and not the past perfect tense. As such, I am unsure whether this pertains to the metrics that were planned to make the links, or to the metrics that will be used for using this artifact. The artifact contains existing links, and this is thus confusing.
overall_preference_reason: A is great for a quick assessment (i.e., filtering). B is great for more detail.
final_suggestions: That said, the first part of the experiment was confusing, as SILK relies on ML approaches, and it was unclear whether the phases pertain to the ML phases, the construction of the mapping, or how the mapping is supposed to be used. Also, while we should not interpret IRIs, we only had access to them, and I was at times thrown off by the tenses used in them.
